_why: EVERY PERSON'S URL, FROZEN. Written once per person and never recomputed.
build_site_data.py used to mint a slug on every run: a fresh dict, and a
collision resolved with `while s in _slugs.values(): s = base-N`. The N is
ITERATION ORDER, so the moment a namesake is added, corrected or removed
every later namesake's URL shifts. That is not a risk in this archive, it
is a thing that happened: between faa46cd and 73d36bf, six men swapped
URLs with each other.
@I70@       anton-blazevic-2  ->  anton-blazevic-6
@I508751@   anton-blazevic-4  ->  anton-blazevic-2
@I508902@   anton-blazevic-5  ->  anton-blazevic-3
@I511448@   anton-blazevic-6  ->  anton-blazevic-4
Anybody who cited /people/anton-blazevic-2/ now lands on a different man.
THIS FILE IS APPEND-ONLY. The generator reads it, uses what it finds
unchanged, and mints only for an id it has never seen. A slug in here is
never edited and never deleted, because a URL that has been published is a
promise. If a person is removed from the tree their line stays, so the slug
is not handed to somebody else.
Seeded 23 September 2026 from the slugs the site was already serving, so
not one URL moved when the generator began reading it.
The position it implements is the Defranceski archive's, of the same day: a
page is a person, an id is frozen, a name is an index.
